full_judgment:
6. The defendant Nos. 2, 4 and 9, in paragraph No. 7 of their written statements, has asserted that this suit is not maintainable because the plaintiffs did not seek saham with reference to RoR survey or RoR record of rights. Besides, in paragraph No. 11(Kha) of their written statements, these defendants Nos. 2, 4 and 9 have also stated that, the CS suit plots have been divided into RoR plot Nos. Nos. 8407, 8408, 8409, 8410, 8411 and 8412 and that as per mutation khatian No. 7528, the plaintiffs have no title in the suit property and that the instant suit is false and ill-advised. It also appears that, the defendant Nos. 2, 4 and 9 had filed better statement on 12-7-2000. 

 10. The trial court, after hearing the parties and having assessed the oral and documentary evidences on record, allowed the suit by its judgment and decree dated 28-9-2000, and directed to make partition of the suit property on the basis of CS khatian and CS plot numbers for the reason, (as recorded his judgment) that, "যেহেতু নালিশী দাগের আর ও আর খতিয়ান ও দাগ নং দ্বারা বাদীর নালিশী জোত চিহ্নিত করা সম্ভব হয় নাই তাই বাদীও সাহাম প্রাপ্ত বিবাদীগণের ওয়ারিশ সিএস খতিয়ান ও দাগ নং দ্বারাই নির্ধারণ করা হইল।" However, it is to be noted here that, the suit property had no boundary to specify or identify the same. 

 13. Learned Advocate Mr Tanvir Parvez appeared for the petitioners. He, having placed the petition, judgments of both the courts below, the evidence adduced by the parties and other materials on record, first of all submits that, one Bhagoban Bosak was owner of the CS plot No. 5685 of CS khatain No. 2700, under Mouza Kishoregonj [Exhibit 1(Ka)j comprising 0.63 acres of land. Bhagoban Bosah had sold and handed over possession of 0.1750 acres of land, out of 0.63 acres of land of CS plot No. 5685, in the year 1923, to one Gopinath Bosak. But, the valuation of the property, in 1923, being less than Taka 100 (one hundred), no kabala was required to be made, or required to be registered. However, Gopinath Bosak having acquired title and possession in 0.1750 acres of land, in a separated portion of the suit property, he had constructed his dwelling hut thereon and had been enjoying the same for more than 12 years, peacefully and without any interruption or objection from any quarter. He proceeds on that, said Gopinath Bosak died in the year 1945 (i.e. before SA/RoR operation) leaving his only daughter Sorola Sundori as the sole heir and she became owner of that 0.1750 acres of land by inheritance and that, the name of Sorala Shundhari Bosak, daughter of Gopinath Boshak, has been recorded in SA/RoR khatian No. 7157 of Mouja, Kishorgonj (Exhibit-গ১), 	alongwith Krishnadhan Boshak and Gyananda Shundari, each having one third shares in the corresponding SA/RoR Plot Nos. 8407, 8408, 8409, 8410, 8411 and 8412 of Mouza Kishoregonj. His further contention is that, Sorala Sundori, as the SA/RoR recorded owner, was enjoying the suit property on payment of rents to the Government and that, the defendant No. 2 was her nephew. He next submits that, while Sorala Sundori, having good title and possession in 0.1750 acres of land, she has sold the same to the defendant No.. 2, by a sale deed No. 450 dated 19- 1-1973, mentioning the SA /RoR plot Nos. 8407, 8408, 8409, 8410, 8411 and 8412 [Exhibit গ(২)]. He points out that, the division of the said CS plots into 6 SA/RoR plots, vide SA/RoR Khatian No. 7157 (Exhibit-গ১) has been also admitted by the contesting defendants Nos. 2, 4 and 9, at paragraph No.12 (kha) of their written statement. This SA khatian (Exhibit-গ১) duly recording name of Sorola Shundari Boshak, has not been disputed, nor the 6 RoR (SA) Plots mentioned in Exhibit-std has been referred to in the schedule of the plaint for the purpose of identification or saham of the suit property, nor the genealogy of the CS recorded owner, nor the chain of title from CS survey has been shown in the plaint with deliberate intent to suppress the actual SA/RoR recorded owners, wherein names of the plaintiffs do not appear. He next submits that, the defendant No 2 has prayed for mutation of his purchased 0.1750 acres of land in his name, vide DCR No.0904622 dated 13-11-1986 BS [Exhibit গ৩ক] and got mutation khatain No. 9302 on 06-11-2006 [Exhibit গ৩ক] and has also paid Khajna [Exhibit ৩(খ)]. He continues that, this defendant No. 2 has specifically stated his case about acquiring title by purchase in 0.1750 acres of land, by giving a clear chin of title and about the subsequent steps taken after purchasing 0.1750 acres of land. Besides, the defendant No. 2 has also adduced adequate and relevant documentary and oral evidences to prove his case, as to prove his title, in the suit property, that comprises 0.1750 acres (or 17 decimals) of homestead land in SA Plot No. 8411 and 0.001 acre (one decimal) of land (Rasta) from SA Plot No. 8412, as recorded in the mutation khatian No. 9302 [Exhibit গ৩ক], prepared in his name. He proceeds on that, PW 1 has admitted the title of this defendant in the suit property. But, without at all considering these documentary and oral evidences, consistently supporting the case of the petitioner, the trial court had decreed the suit. Moreso, without considering that, no identification of the suit property with reference to RoR or SA survey or with any specific boundary was given in the schedule to the plaint and in the absence of any proof that, the plaintiffs were the heirs of the CS recorded owner, the trial court had decreed the suit and also gave saham to them in respect of the unidentified suit property with reference to CS khatian and CS plots and ignoring the duly proved registered title deed No. 450 dated 19-1-1973 [Exhibit st4 covering 0.1750 acres of land owned by the defendant No. 2. He proceeds on that, when the defendant No. 2 has proved the 'SA/RoR khatian No. 7157 [Exhibit গ১] proving prima-facie title of his bia and his title deed Exhibit [Exhibit গ২] in respect of 0.1750 acres of land purchased by him alongwith the duly proved DCR, khatain and rent receipt (Exhibit 3 series) and the execution of the sale deed Exhibit [Exhibit গ২] being proved by an attesting witness (PW 6) and his possession in the suit property also being proved by adducing adequate evidence, the trial court ought to have rejected the plaint or ought not to have decreed the suit by allotting shares in respect of 0.1750 acres of land owned by the defendant No. 2 or even in respect of the rest portion of the unspecific and unidentified property described on the basis of CS record, while there was no proof that the plaintiffs and other defendants claiming saham by way of inheritance were actually the heirs of CS recorded owner. Besides, the trial court had totally ignored the fact that, no chain of title of the plaintiff has been narrated in the plaint, from CS to RoR survey, no chain of title given in support of the claim for partition. He then submits that, in spite of disclosure of and even after knowing about title deed of the defendant No. 2, the said deed was not challenged by the plaintiffs, nor they have filed any suit for declaration of title in respect of 0.1750 acres of land claimed by the defendant No. 2, nor the plaintiffs have prayed for correction of the record of right (SA/RoR Khatian Exhibit I)), prepared in the name of Sorala Sundari Bosak, daughter of Gopinath Bosak. The learned Advocate then points out that, even the mutation khatian No. 9302 [Exhibit গ৩ক] existing in the name of the defendant No. 2, remained un¬assailed. In support of his contention, the learned Advocate has referred to the decision reported in 49 DLR (AD) 68: between Rezaul Karin and others vs Shamsuzzoha and others, wherein in it has been held that, without filing title suit, in such a situation, the simple suit for partition was not maintainable. He has also referred to another decision reported in 4 BLC 195: between Shahani Bibi being dead her heirs Mohammad Azim and other vs Nur Islam being dead his heirs Doly Islam and others, wherein it has been held that, the deposition given by the son or given by the father was not admissible as evidence as because the deponent's son did not have any power of attorney and the judgment was given upon a detailed discussion of section 120 of the Evidence Act as well as of Rules 1 and 2 of Order HI of the Code of Civil Procedure. Therefore, the deposition of PW 1 was not admissible in evidence as per the decision given in 4 BLC 195. So, he maintains that, there is no substantive evidence supporting plaintiff's case, the corroborative evidence of other PWs has no value. Next, referring to the deposition of the plaintiff's witnesses as well as to that of the defendants, the learned Advocate submits that, the defendant's possession has been admitted by the PW 1 and this fact has been duly corroborated by the DWs. In this view of the facts and circumstances, the learned Advocate maintains that, in passing the impugned judgment and decree dated 20-11-2007, the trial court has committed grave error of law causing serious prejudice to the defendant No. 2, who has lawful title in 0.1750 acres of land. On the other hand, he submits, the appellate court, as the last court of fact, without himself indepen¬dently considering the evidence on record has mechanically upheld the judgment and decree of the trial court and, as such, the judgment and decree of the appellate court is based on misinterpretation of documentary and oral evidences on record and its findings are totally perverse in view of the evidence on record and a defective plaint. Besides, he proceeds on, in passing the impugned judgment and decree, the appellate court has travelled beyond its jurisdiction by ignoring the law declared by the Apex Court, as reported in 49 DLR (AD) 68 as well as that of the judgment of the High Court Division, reported 4 BLC 195, which were binding on it as per Article 111 of the Constitution. Therefore, he concludes that, the appellate court has committed grave error of, law, resulting in error in passing the impugned decision, occasioning failure of justice. Hence, the impugned judgment and decree passed by the appellate court, affirming that of the trial court, is liable to be set-aside and the Rule has merits which may kindly be made absolute. 

 16. It is admitted fact that, Bhagoban Bosak was the owner of 0.63 decimals of land lying at CS plot No. 5685 under CS khatian No. 2700 of Mouza Kishoregonj, Porgona Hossenpur, PS Kishoregong District-Mymensingh ([Exhibit ১ক]. The claim of the plaintiff and the defendant Nos. 6, 7(Ka) and 10-13, is that this Bhagoban Bosak is their predecessor and that they were entitled to get saham in respect of 0.2650 acres of land out of 0.63 acres of land lying at CS plot No. 5685 of CS Khatian No. 2700 [Exhibit I (Ka)), recorded in the name of BhagobanBosah. On the other hand, claim of the defendant No. 2 is that CS recorded owner Bhagoban Bosak sold 0.1750 decimals of land, to one Gopinath Bosak, in the year 1923, out of 0.63 acre (63 decimals) of land, that was lying at the east-southern portion of the CS plot 5685. But, the value of the said property was less than Taka 100 (one hundred) at that time (in 1923). Therefore, no formal deed or registration was required pursuant to that sale. However, Gopinath Bosak having got title and possession in 0.1750 acres of CS plot No. 5685, he had built his dwelling but and was enjoying the same peacefully and without any interruption from any quarter. Thereafter, in the year 1945 this Gopinath Bosak had died leaving his only daughter Sorola Sundari Bosak as his only heir and she became successor in respect of 0.1750 acres of land, left by her deceased father Gopinath Bosak. The further case of this defendant No. 2 is that, the daughter of Gopinath Bosak (Sorala Shundari Bosak) had thus been enjoying this 0.1750 acres of land on payment of rents to the Government that she had sold the said property to Indra Mohan Bosak, who is the defendant No. 2 and the present petitioner. During liberation war, their sale deed was lost. However, in his purchased property; this defendant No. 2 had built a wooden hut, a tin-shed but and 2 pacca houses and also planted some trees. It also appears that, he had also applied for mutation of the suit property in his name and accordingly paid fees for mutation and a mutation khatian has been opened in his name and he has paid rents. The concerned DCR, mutation khatian No. 9302 Ga (3) series and rent receipts Exhibit Kha (3). 

 18. I also find that this deposition of DW5 is corroborates the facts recorded in mutation khatian No. 9302 of Mouza Kisghoregonj [Exhibit গ৩ক] describing that in SA/RoR Plot No. 8411 there is a home and 0.17 acres (17 decimals) of land recorded in the name of defendant No. 2 and that, the defendant No. 2 owns 0.001 acre (one decimal) land in SA/RoR plot No. 8412 (Rasta/Path), both totaling 0.1800 acres (or 18 decimals) of land with a dwelling house, as deposed by PW 5. Hence, I find that this PW 5 as a credible witness. 

 21. I also find that, in spite of disclosure of and even after knowing about the registered title deed of the defendant No. 2 [Exhibit গ২], the said deed was not challenged by the plaintiffs, nor they have filed any suit for declaration of title in respect of 0.1750 acres of land claimed by the defendant No. 2 on the basis of his title deed, nor the plaintiffs have prayed for correction of the record of right (SA/RoR Khatian Exhibit গ১), prepared in the name of Sorala Sundari Bosak, daughter of Gopinath Bosak. Thus, I find that, even the mutation khatian No. 9302 [Exhibit .গ৩ক] existing in the name of the defendant No. 2, remained un-assailed. 

 25. Therefore, I find and hold that, the deed No. 450 dated 19-1-1973 (Exhibit গ২) has been duly proved as per section 68 of the Evidence Act, 1872, by an attesting witness (PW 6). The deed No. 450 dated 19-1-1973 (Exhibit গ২) has made clear reference to the CS plot and CS khatian as well as to the hal or S.A /RoR khatian No. 7157, JL No. 170, Mouza Kishoregonj, District Mymensingh, referring to SA/RoR plot Nos. 8407, 8408, 8409, 8410, 8411 and 8412, where I find that, Sorola Sundari is one of the 3 (three) owners, recorded in that khatian, all of them jointly owing 16 annas in the aforesaid 6 (six) SA/RoR plot Nos. 8407, 8408, 8409, 8410, 8411 and 8412. 

 27. It is to be noted here that, the name of the plaintiffs and other co-sharers, by inheritance or otherwise appear in the latest SA/RoR khatina.  No decree can be passed by the trial court in this suit, when it admits that, the suit property is not identifiable with SA/RoR plots or khatian. 

 28. Nor any saharn can be given in respect of an unspecified property. The trial court in its judgment has recorded that, the suit property is not identifiable with reference to the RoR or SA  khatain, although both the courts below are silent  about non-identification of suit property for lacking any boundary and for lack of any  reference to the latest survey or khatian bearing names of the plaintiffs as the tenants, and both the courts below have failed to appreciate that no unidentified property can be partitioned. 

 29. Besides, there is no chain from the CS khatian to SA or RoR Khatian or with reference to latest survey and plot numbers. There is no proof that the plaintiffs or of the defendants, who are claiming saham by inheritance, were the actual heirs of the CS recorded owners. Even, SA/RoR records were not placed or proved before the trial court to show that they had interest in the suit property or that they are co-sharers in the suit property. 

 31. PW 1 admits the existence of subsequent survey and the division of CS plots in 6 SA/RoR khatian, but has suppressed the subsequent changes in respect of the devolution or change of ownership in the original CS plots. But, the courts below have made no observation or finding as to what was the basis before them to admit the plaintiff and some other defendants (claiming share by way of inheritance) were the true and only heirs of the CS recorded owner, moreso, in view of the specific and proved case of the defendant No. 2. 

 35. In these circumstances, both the courts below have shown not only the lack of knowledge that this partition suit was not maintainable with reference to CS khatian and no saham with reference to CS plots or in respect of unidentified property could be given. The courts below cannot presume that, there has been no change in respect of CS plots or their quantity, nature or in respect of ownership after 1920 (when CS was done), moreso, when there is no chain of title to show the devolution of ownership to these plaintiffs and the defendants Nos. 6, 7Ka and 10.13 from 1920 (CS operation).
